title: Moroni Finishes the Record
summary: Moroni says he is finishing his father’s record and has only a few things left to write as commanded by his father.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni finishes his father Mormon’s record and has few things to write, commanded by his father.

unspecified_visual_details: Moroni’s appearance, writing materials, and surroundings.

narration.text: Behold I, Moroni, do finish the record of my father, Mormon.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Mormon as present; he is mentioned as Moroni’s father.

title: The Survivors Are Hunted
summary: After the battle at Cumorah, Nephites who escaped southward are hunted by the Lamanites until all are destroyed.

explicit_facts.text: After the battle at Cumorah, the Nephites who escaped southward were hunted by the Lamanites until all were destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanites pursuing the escaping Nephites.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the landscape, combatants, and any specific pursuit or destruction actions.

narration.text: the Nephites who had escaped into the country southward were hunted by the Lamanites

prohibited_inventions: Do not show a specific killing or battle action not narrated in this verse.

title: Moroni Remains Alone
summary: Moroni says his father was killed, his people are gone, and he remains alone to write their destruction, uncertain whether he will be slain.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni’s father was killed, Moroni remains alone, and his people are gone.
Moroni does not know whether he will be slain.

unspecified_visual_details: Moroni’s surroundings and appearance.

narration.text: I even remain alone to write the sad tale of the destruction of my people.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Mormon’s death as a present action; it is reported in narration.

title: Moroni Plans to Hide the Record
summary: Moroni says he will write and hide the records in the earth. He has no ore, is alone, and has no friends or destination.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni will write and hide the records in the earth.
Moroni says he has no ore, is alone, has no friends, and nowhere to go.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni with the record, contemplating its concealment.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether he is actively burying anything, and the location, tools, and appearance of the record.

narration.text: I will write and hide up the records in the earth

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The planned hiding is not yet narrated as an action taking place.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the record already buried.

title: Four Hundred Years Have Passed
summary: Moroni states that four hundred years have passed since the coming of the Lord and Savior.

explicit_facts.text: Four hundred years have passed since the coming of the Lord and Savior.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visual representation of the passage of time.

narration.text: four hundred years have passed away since the coming of our Lord and Savior.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Lord and Savior appearing; this verse only refers to the passage of time.

title: The Nephites Are No More
summary: Moroni recounts that the Lamanites hunted the Nephites from place to place until they were no more. He says the Lamanites are at war among themselves and the land is marked by continual murder and bloodshed.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites hunted the Nephites from city to city and place to place until the Nephites were no more.
The Lamanites are at war with one another, and the land is described as a continual round of murder and bloodshed.
Moroni attributes the destruction to the hand of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A visual of the land or ruined settlements may accompany Moroni’s account.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific cities, battles, victims, and any visible divine hand.

narration.text: the Lamanites have hunted my people, the Nephites, down from city to city
the Lamanites are at war one with another

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The hand of the Lord is stated as an explanation, not described as a visible figure or event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict blood, gore, or a literal visible hand of the Lord.

title: Those Who Remain on the Land
summary: Moroni says only the Lamanites and robbers exist on the land, and that only Jesus’s disciples know the true God. The disciples’ current whereabouts are unknown.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says none remain on the land except the Lamanites and robbers.
The disciples of Jesus knew the true God, but no one knows whether they are still on the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni writing alone as he recounts who remains.
unspecified_visual_details: The location or appearance of the Lamanites, robbers, and disciples.

narration.text: there are none save it be the Lamanites and robbers that do exist upon the face of the land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The disciples are spoken of in reported narration and are not necessarily present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the disciples as present; their whereabouts are explicitly unknown.

title: The Disciples Ministered to Moroni and Mormon
summary: Moroni says that he and his father saw the disciples, who ministered to them.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni and his father saw the disciples, and the disciples ministered to them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The disciples ministering to Moroni and Mormon.
unspecified_visual_details: When and where this occurred, the disciples’ number and appearance, and what their ministry involved.

narration.text: my father and I have seen them, and they have ministered unto us.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent what the disciples said or did as part of their ministry.

title: Moroni Addresses Those Who Receive the Record
summary: Moroni addresses whoever receives the record, saying that one who does not condemn its imperfections will know greater things. He identifies himself as Mormon’s son and a descendant of Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says a recipient who does not condemn the record’s imperfections will know greater things.
Moroni identifies himself as Mormon’s son and a descendant of Nephi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni writing directly to future readers.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance or setting of any future recipient.

narration.text: whoso receiveth this record, and shall not condemn it because of the imperfections which are in it

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The recipient is addressed in the record and need not be depicted.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a future reader as present.

title: The Record Is to Be Brought to Light
summary: Moroni says he hides the record by God’s command, that it is not to be used for gain, and that only God can empower its emergence. He declares it will come from the earth to the knowledge of the people by God’s power.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says he hides the record by the Lord’s command and that no one shall have the plates to get gain.
The record can be brought to light only through power given by God, for God’s glory or the welfare of the covenant people.
The record shall come out of the earth and into the knowledge of the people by the power of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni with the record as he writes about its future emergence.
unspecified_visual_details: The method, place, and time of its future emergence.

narration.text: it shall be brought out of the earth

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The record emerging is a future promise, not an event occurring in the present scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a future finder or the record physically emerging now.

title: Warnings Against Condemnation and Demands
summary: Moroni warns against condemning the record or demanding it under threat. He teaches that rash judgment and violence will be answered by the Lord, whose are judgment and vengeance.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni warns that one who condemns the record should beware of danger of hell fire.
Moroni warns against demanding that the record be shown under threat of smiting.
Moroni says the rash judge will be judged rashly and the one who smites will be smitten by the Lord.
Moroni quotes scripture that judgment and vengeance belong to the Lord.

unspecified_visual_details: Any condemned person or threatened encounter.

narration.text: man shall not smite, neither shall he judge

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Warnings and teachings are conveyed as writing, not staged as a confrontation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unnamed person threatening Moroni.

title: The Lord’s Work Will Continue
summary: Moroni warns those who oppose the Lord’s work and covenant people, and declares that the Lord’s eternal purposes will continue until all promises are fulfilled.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni warns those who speak wrathfully against the Lord’s work and covenant people.
The Lord’s eternal purposes will continue until all promises are fulfilled.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni writing his warning and declaration.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visual representation of the Lord’s purposes continuing.

narration.text: the eternal purposes of the Lord shall roll on

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Roll on” is figurative language, not a literal depicted event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict people being hewn down or cast into fire; the wording is a warning.

title: The Saints Cry from the Dust
summary: Moroni urges readers to search Isaiah’s prophecies and says earlier saints who possessed the land will cry to the Lord from the dust. He recounts their prayers and faith, and says their prayers included the person who would bring the record forth.

explicit_facts.text: The earlier saints who possessed the land will cry to the Lord from the dust, and the Lord will remember his covenant with them.
Their prayers were for their brethren, and they had faith in the Lord’s name.
Their prayers were also for the person the Lord would allow to bring the record forth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni writing about earlier saints and their prayers.
unspecified_visual_details: The saints’ identities, appearances, and the time and place of their prayers.

narration.text: even from the dust will they cry unto the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The saints are described in prophecy and recollection, not necessarily shown as present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the listed miraculous acts as present events; they are reported as past acts of faith.

title: The Record Will Come Forth
summary: Moroni declares that the record will come out of the earth by the hand of the Lord, in a time when people say miracles have ceased, and that it will be as if someone spoke from the dead.

explicit_facts.text: The record will come out of the earth by the hand of the Lord and cannot be stopped.
It will come when people say miracles are done away, as if one should speak from the dead.

unspecified_visual_details: The future setting and manner in which the record comes forth.

narration.text: for out of the earth shall they come

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “As if one should speak from the dead” is a comparison, not a literal visible resurrection.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a dead person speaking or the future emergence as a current event.

title: A Future Day Foretold
summary: The verses foretell a day of secret combinations and works of darkness, denial of God’s power, defiled and prideful churches, and reports of fires, tempests, smoke, wars, and earthquakes.

explicit_facts.text: The blood of saints shall cry unto the Lord because of secret combinations and works of darkness.
The power of God shall be denied; churches shall become defiled and prideful, and church leaders and teachers shall rise in pride and envy those who belong to their churches.
Fires, tempests, and vapors of smoke in foreign lands shall be heard of.
Wars, rumors of wars, and earthquakes in divers places shall be heard of.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophecy can be presented through text without depicting its foretold events as occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: Typography, layout, and background for the quoted text.

narration.text: And it shall come in a day when the blood of saints shall cry unto the Lord, because of secret combinations and the works of darkness.
And there shall also be heard of wars, rumors of wars, and earthquakes in divers places.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses foretell a future day; they do not narrate these events as presently occurring.
The blood of saints crying unto the Lord is not a basis for depicting literal speaking blood.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify or depict an unnamed speaker.
Do not depict the foretold disasters, conflicts, or blood as present-tense events.
Do not invent specific people, places, or incidents.

title: Warnings Against Iniquity and Gain
summary: Moroni foretells widespread pollution and wrongdoing, churches offering forgiveness for money, and people building churches for gain and altering God’s word. He urges readers to look to God’s revelations.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni foretells pollution, murders, robbery, lying, deceit, and other abominations.
He foretells churches saying forgiveness is offered for money.
Moroni asks why people build churches for gain and alter God’s holy word, and urges them to look to God’s revelations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni writing a warning to future readers.
unspecified_visual_details: The future churches, people, and acts described.

narration.text: churches built up that shall say: Come unto me, and for your money you shall be forgiven of your sins.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future conduct is prophesied, not shown as a contemporary event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a church, preacher, or transaction as a present scene.

title: Moroni Speaks to Future Readers
summary: Moroni says the Lord has shown him great things about what will shortly come, and that he speaks to readers as if they were present though they are not. He says Jesus Christ has shown those readers to him and that he knows their doing.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord has shown Moroni great things concerning what must shortly come.
Moroni speaks to his readers as if present, though they are not, and says Jesus Christ has shown them to him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni writing directly to future readers.
unspecified_visual_details: How Jesus Christ showed the readers to Moroni, and any appearance involved.

narration.text: I speak unto you as if ye were present, and yet ye are not.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse mentions Jesus Christ but does not describe a visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Jesus Christ or future readers as visibly present.

title: Pride and Neglect of the Needy
summary: Moroni rebukes his addressees for pride, valuing wealth and adornment above people in need, and failing to notice those in need.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says that nearly all of his addressees lift themselves up in pride, and that their churches have become polluted because of that pride.
Moroni says the addressees love money, possessions, fine apparel, and church adornment more than the poor, needy, sick, and afflicted.
Moroni questions teachers about polluting the holy church of God, being ashamed to take upon them the name of Christ, and seeking the praise of the world.
Moroni asks why the addressees adorn themselves while the hungry, needy, naked, sick, and afflicted pass by unnoticed.

unspecified_visual_details: Moroni’s appearance and surroundings.
The addressees’ appearance and surroundings.

narration.text: And I know that ye do walk in the pride of your hearts;
Why do ye adorn yourselves with that which hath no life, and yet suffer the hungry, and the needy, and the naked, and the sick and the afflicted to pass by you, and notice them not?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The first-person narrator is Moroni, son of Mormon, as specified for this chapter.
These verses are Moroni’s rebuke and questions; they do not narrate an encounter occurring before the viewer.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an invented encounter between the addressees and people in need.
Do not give unnamed addressees invented identities or biographies.
Do not depict an unstated divine appearance or literalize figurative language.
Do not quote or stage events from verses outside the supplied passage.

title: Widows and Orphans Cry to the Lord
summary: Moroni condemns teachers who seek worldly praise and asks why people build secret abominations for gain, causing widows and orphans to mourn and the blood of their slain relatives to cry to the Lord. He warns that vengeance will come.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni asks why teachers pollute God’s church and are ashamed to take Christ’s name for worldly praise.
He says secret abominations for gain cause widows and orphans to mourn and the blood of their fathers and husbands to cry to the Lord.
Moroni warns that vengeance will come upon those responsible for the blood of the saints.

unspecified_visual_details: The people, secret acts, widows, orphans, and circumstances described.

narration.text: the sword of vengeance hangeth over you

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “The sword of vengeance” is figurative warning language, not a literal visible sword.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal sword hanging over people or stage the future violence.
